data.narrative: Module 6 added cache-aside Redis caching to the redirect hot path with graceful DB fallback. The BREAK introduced a stale-cache bug (DELETE path missing invalidation) which was reproduced live, root-caused to the write path, fixed, and locked down with three regression tests. End-to-end verification covered cache miss/hit, update invalidation, and a Redis-down fallback drill.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose cache-aside (A) with quantified reasoning: read-dominated hot path means populate-on-miss + delete-on-write, avoiding write-path coupling to Redis health that write-through would impose.
dimension_scores.evidence: "the redirect hot path is read-dominated ... we only populate the cache on a miss and invalidate (delete the key) on update/delete - no write-path overhead"

dimension_scores.observation: Closed the loop end-to-end: reproduced stale redirect after delete, hypothesized missing invalidation, confirmed in code, restored the invalidate call, and added a regression test proving the cached key is gone and redirect returns 404.
dimension_scores.evidence: repro: delete 204 then /r/<code> still 302; fix verified by test_delete_invalidates_cache; full suite 38 passed

dimension_scores.observation: Restricted caching to public redirect targets only and explicitly rejected caching auth-protected data, avoiding cross-user leakage and revocation gaps.
dimension_scores.evidence: "we only cache public redirect targets (code->long_url), never owner-scoped rows"

dimension_scores.observation: Designed for failure: Redis-down drill proved redirects keep working via Postgres fallback with no hang; TTL kept as expiration safety net; protocol=2 compatibility fixed a silent cache outage.
dimension_scores.evidence: stopped redis-server, /r/def456 still 302 via DB fallback, redis restarted cleanly

dimension_scores.observation: Explained cache invalidation difficulty, auth-cache risks, and Redis-down behavior concisely and tied them to the module's decision.
dimension_scores.evidence: VERIFY responses named invalidation spread across write paths, TTL as safety net, and graceful degradation

strengths: Caught that redis-py 8 defaults to RESP3 HELLO which Redis 5 rejects, so caching was silently failing - fixed with protocol=2 instead of papering over it
Closed the stale-cache bug with a full regression suite (3 new tests) plus live repro and post-fix verification
Executed the Redis-down drill end-to-end (stop, verify DB fallback, restart)
data.recommendation: Next module: background jobs for analytics - keep the graceful-degradation pattern (queue down must not block redirects) and consider a thundering-herd guard (cache stampede coalescing) as a follow-up hardening step.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented cache-aside caching with invalidation on write paths and verified it end-to-end.
public_evidence.technical_detail: api/app/services/cache.py + redirect and links routers: get/set/invalidate_redirect_target, protocol=2 client, TTL 300s.
public_evidence.proof: create -> redirect 302 (cache miss+populate, key redirect:<code> in Redis) -> second redirect 302 (cache hit) -> PATCH -> redirect returns new URL; delete -> redirect 404
public_evidence.ability: Builds and verifies cache correctness under failure
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows production-grade caching: invalidation discipline, graceful degradation, and regression coverage.

public_evidence.student_action: Wrote three regression tests guarding stale-cache behavior for update, delete, and cache-hit paths.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves correctness is locked by tests, not just verified once.

stale-cache bug root-caused and fixed with delete-path invalidation
